title: Tech Support: How to change the boot order on an Intel Motherboard
description: Micro Center Tech Support shows you how to change the boot sequence on an Intel Motherboard. http://www.microcentertech.com

asr.full_text: Are you having problems changing your boot sequence? on your Intel motherboard? This is Paul from TX here at Microscenter. Today I want to show you how to go into the BIOS and change the boot sequence Let's get started. Start this process with the computer completely turned off. Let's go ahead and turn it back on waiting for the splash screen and in this case it's an Intel motherboard we hit F2 to enter the BIOS. In other cases, it is an escape or F1. All right. Now we want to use the arrow key and arrow over to the boot section. The second section down is the boot device priority. That is what we want to change. Right now it is set optical drive first, removable drive second, hard disk drive third, and network is fourth. To change that, hit Enter, and the minus key or the shift plus key to move the device up and down, changing the priority of the boot. Let's say you're reloading Windows and you want to boot off of that CD-ROM. You want to set optical drivers first, so it will actually ask you as it's booting up, do you want to boot off with the CD-ROM, hit any key ,you hit a key in we'll boot off the CD-ROM and then start your Windows install process. So once you have the change that you like let's go ahead over to exit saving changes click on yes now you can put it boot-up using the new bootorder that you just set. if you have any other questions come visit us at www.microcentretech.com

The speaker gives concrete keyboard and menu instructions, and the screen shows the corresponding Boot Device Priority settings. Micro Center Tech branding and an informational website outro further frame the presentation as organizational support content.
